Any “truth” we adopt is always based on perspective and of course, some assumptions. Perspective is an interesting subject since it can take so many different forms. By way of example, let me describe some things truthfully from two perspectives with two assumptions:

Perspective 1 The item is constructed out of wood with finely engraved patterns. The surface is flat with a soft cushion perpendicular to it covering some spindles that rise up from its surface. There is nothing underneath to give it support, and it is apparently floating in the air and not fixed to any surface . Perspective 2 The item is constructed out of wood and is very plain with no carvings or designs. It has four spindles that hang from it at a slight angle such that each spindle points ever so slightly away from each other at the four corners. Between each spindle are wooden rods that are attached between each spindle and form a sort of box. On the bottom of each spindle is some sort of metal object affixed to it with a screw.

Two perspectives that are quite different yet they actually are describing the same object (a chair). The first is looking straight down on the chair and the second is underneath looking straight up. EXPERIENCING THE TRUTH The truth of the matter is that no human being is immune from perspective.
